result.response:
The bug has been identified and fixed according to the requirements specified in `summary.txt`.

### Cause of the Issue
In [`MathUtils.equals(double x, double y)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/util/MathUtils.java#L416-L418), the method returned `(Double.isNaN(x) && Double.isNaN(y)) || x == y`. This violated the specification in two ways:
1. It considered two `Double.NaN` values equal to each other, whereas the requirement dictates that any comparison involving `Double.NaN` must return `false` (in contrast to `equalsIncludingNaN`).
2. It performed `x == y` instead of allowing adjacent floating-point values separated by at most 1 ULP as specified by `equals(x, y, 1)`.

Consequently, array comparisons such as `MathUtils.equals(new double[] { Double.NaN }, new double[] { Double.NaN })` incorrectly evaluated to `true`.

### Solution
Updated [`MathUtils.equals(double x, double y)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/util/MathUtils.java#L416-L418) to delegate to `equals(x, y, 1)` as documented in its Javadoc and requirement specification:
```java
public static boolean equals(double x, double y) {
    return equals(x, y, 1);
}
```

### Verification
- Tested with `org.apache.commons.math.util.MathUtilsTest` (including `testArrayEquals`), and all 61 tests passed without errors.
- Generated focused patch file [`nl_fix.patch`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_b_fix/nl_fix.patch).
